author: reek
body: This path already failed at CHECK before 2026-07-28, so the change here is not the refusal but WHAT IT SAID. It raised two diagnostics and both were false:

author: reek
body: The record is declared `mutable`, and it does have that field. The empty name in the first is the same missing strip: the type-name lookup reads RecordTy and ConstructedTy and answers "" for anything else, so the wrapper produced a message about a type with no name.

author: reek
body: **What this test CANNOT check, stated so nobody reads more into a green than is there.** A `.failing` sidecar requires each listed code to appear; it cannot require that no OTHER code appears. So this pin catches the refusal disappearing or changing code, and it would NOT catch CDX2060 and CDX2005 coming back alongside it. The single- diagnostic property was verified by hand on the compiler that shipped this change and is not under a runner.
